paper.title_en: Exploring the effect of intrinsic decoherence on the quantum correlations in $2\otimes 3$ Heisenberg chains exposed to inhomogeneous magnetic field
paper.abstract_en: While the effects of intrinsic decoherence on homogeneous Heisenberg spin chains are widely documented, hybrid lower-dimensional architectures remain less explored. In this work, we investigate a heterogeneous quantum system comprising a spin-1 (qutrit) and a spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ (qubit) coupled under the influence of an inhomogeneous magnetic field. Under the assumption that the system originates from an initial thermal state, we derive an exact analytical solution for the density matrix using the Milburn master equation. We monitor the dynamical evolution of several key quantumness measures including geometric quantum discord, von Neumann entropy, and concurrence with a particular focus on how intrinsic decoherence reshapes their temporal profiles. Our numerical and analytical results demonstrate that robust quantum correlations and high-degree entanglement can be successfully generated and preserved by carefully tuning both the decoherence rate and the magnetic field inhomogeneity parameter. Furthermore, we test the ultimate bounds of parameter estimation within this framework by evaluating the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI). The results reveal that estimation precision is highly sensitive to both the relative magnitude of the parameters and the specific QFI metric employed. Crucially, optimal estimation accuracy remains strictly confined to early interaction intervals, experiencing severe degradation as the system evolves toward its long-time steady state.
